title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned No reply yet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: No reply yet
options.thesis: Today is who still has not come back. The person you are about to nudge sits closest.
options.viewport: A phone column. The first line is who you are waiting on, the ask sits under the name, and the next nudge sits at the trailing edge. Opening that row lets the others step back.
options.risk: One timid pass and it is the Phone app: small names, icon buttons, and no record that you followed up.

raised.raise: The nudge is written in words, and the person you are about to ask carries one mark the others do not.
Whether they still have it changes the row’s posture. There is no status pill.
Opening a row clears the rest of the queue so one conversation holds the line.
The person you are about to nudge is larger and closer. Nobody sits in a card.

options.label: Rolodex
options.thesis: Each card is a person who still has the ask. The corner date is when you will nudge them.
options.viewport: One card fills the phone. The name is the headline, the ask is the body, and the other due people show only as tabs behind it.
options.risk: A rolodex is the familiar object this kind of brief reaches for, and it turns into paper nostalgia if the next follow-up is not obvious.

options.label: Plate sheet
options.thesis: Each plate is a person who still has the thing, and the stamp records that you nudged them.
options.viewport: One near-white sheet. A few ruled rows, the next check as a small credit, and a stamp where the touch was just logged.
options.case: The stamp makes a logged touch visible in a way a phone list does not. A design annual is not where you live, so the sheet is less yours.
options.risk: Registration marks crowd a four-row phone queue.

options.label: Departure board
options.thesis: Each row is someone who still has the thing. The time column is when you will ask again.
options.viewport: A steel frame, three ruled rows, the name and ask in flap cells, the next moment in a fixed time column.
options.case: The time column makes “when you’ll ask again” the structure of the screen. A public concourse is not a private list of people you are waiting on.
options.risk: Delay lamps would scold, so they are refused. The board can still feel like a station if the type shouts.

options.label: Stockroom tag
options.thesis: Each open ask keeps a tag on until they deliver it.
options.viewport: Quoted labels and a hazard stripe across the row that is not yours to touch.
options.case: Hazard stripes and stockroom quotes are not how you follow up with a person, and they crowd the phone.
options.kept: Name the action in words, and mark the active item with one token.
options.risk: It reads as a warning label.

options.label: Tensegrity column
options.lineage: A kinetic sculpture of rods and cord
options.thesis: The outcome stands only while each person’s ask holds tension.
options.viewport: A network of members you trace from a person to the force holding them.
options.case: A force diagram is the dependency graph this product refuses, and a sculpture is not your morning queue.
options.kept: State is a change in posture, not a badge.
options.risk: The task disappears into the structure.

options.label: Crew terminal
options.thesis: Today is one typed query about who still has not delivered.
options.viewport: Green capitals type on one line at a time, with an amber plate for trouble.
options.case: A crew terminal is a fiction, and amber danger scolds a late reply.
options.kept: The second step takes the whole line. The rest of the queue waits.
options.risk: Nostalgia and alarm replace the people.

options.label: Depth queue
options.thesis: The person you are about to nudge is the only line in focus. The rest recede.
options.viewport: One ivory line holds still on a black void while dimmer lines drift behind it.
options.case: A demoscene void is not your daily scene, and hidden controls fail a two-tap follow-up.
options.kept: The person you are waiting on is larger and closer, and never sits in a box.
options.risk: Illegible the moment a second step needs a control.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A to-do list of follow-ups, with checkboxes, due dates, and a sidebar of lists.
canonCard.viewport: A left rail of lists, checkbox rows, a date column, and a round add button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every task app, including the red dates this product exists to refuse.
